A DBS check is a background check that reveals any criminal convictions, cautions, reprimands, or warnings. The level of check required depends on the role: Standard DBS : Checks for spent and unspent convictions, cautions, reprimands, and final warnings. Enhanced DBS : Includes the above, plus any additional information held by local police thats considered relevant to the role. Who Needs a DBS Check Most roles involving direct patient contact, working with children or vulnerable adults, or access to sensitive information will require a DBS check. The Costs for a DBS At Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT), roles that require a DBS check are subject to a cost recovery policy. description: This is a key role within our multidisciplinary team, supporting clinicians by ensuring incoming clinical correspondence is reviewed, processed and accurately recorded. You will identify relevant clinical information, update patient records and ensure correspondence is directed to the right person or team. The role will suit someone who enjoys working with detailed information, follows processes carefully and can use their judgement to identify what can be safely managed and what needs clinical input. You will help reduce unnecessary GP workload while recognising when something is outside your remit and needs to be escalated. Day-to-day work may include reviewing hospital letters, investigation results and other clinical correspondence, extracting and coding relevant information, updating patient records, filing documentation and directing tasks to the appropriate team. You may also support note summarising and other activities that maintain clear, accurate clinical records. Accuracy and patient safety are at the heart of this role. You will need to manage your workload, follow practice and national guidance, and know when to seek advice from a GP, supervisor or manager. By ensuring clinical information is handled accurately, promptly and safely, you will help our clinicians work effectively and support patient care. As a Clinical Administrator, you will help keep the practices clinical and administrative processes running smoothly. Your main duties will include processing incoming clinical correspondence, accurately updating patient records, reviewing and coding clinical information, and ensuring information is directed to the appropriate team member. You will support the processing of hospital and clinic letters, results, safeguarding information and electronic data, as well as summarising new patient records, supporting registrations and managing out-of-area correspondence. Working closely with the clinical team, you will identify and escalate complex or sensitive issues appropriately and support effective communication across the practice. You will also contribute to team meetings and training and help new colleagues learn practice processes. High standards of confidentiality, information governance and accuracy are essential. Job Summary The Clinical Administrator provides vital support to the multidisciplinary team by managing and processing clinical correspondence and patient records in line with practice and national guidelines. The post-holder will work as part of the Clinical Administration team, prioritising their workload effectively, maintaining strict confidentiality at all times, and knowing when to escalate matters to supervisors or clinicians. Roles and Responsibilities Ensure all incoming and internal correspondence is stored in patient records. Review and Read Code clinical correspondence before forwarding to clinicians. Process and file hospital letters, reports, emails and other correspondence. Code diagnoses, procedures and investigations accurately. Summarise new patient records (manual and GP2GP) and process registrations, transfers, and out-of-area notifications. Manage incoming test results, redirect unmatched pathology, and process screening and monitoring results. Process Out of Hours reports and other external communications. Monitor the practice email inbox, flagging urgent queries promptly. Provide administrative cover for other team members when necessary. Open, scan, distribute and file post; manage photocopying and record requests. Assist with training and mentoring of new staff. Maintain a tidy office environment and adhere to a clear desk policy.
